answer.answer: Field brief: Little Cloud is a low-threat stop, but bank the valuable excess ammunition and consumables if storage is reasonably close. Then clear Little Cloud methodically and continue to the even lighter Starry Night, opening its final chest before debris-looting. Treat the tagged Regeneration Chamber only as a travel-saving checkpoint—not supply insurance.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 difficulty. Map data shows 13 persistent hostile spawn entries within 250 units: 8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder, with no mapped Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration. These markers represent possible persistent population, not 13 simultaneous attackers; the player's later direct observation was that Little Cloud was “no big deal.”

Bank excess ammunition and consumables first if storage is reasonably quick to reach; otherwise clear Little Cloud methodically, then proceed to Starry Night. The nearby claimed Regeneration Chamber lowers travel risk but does not replace staged replacement equipment and a safe recovery cache.

A claimed Regeneration Chamber is only a respawn point: a prior nearby respawn had no spare weapons or replacement materials and still forced a return to Landerworks. In another observed encounter, corruption disabled the contested base and its Chamber, causing respawn at the starting launcher. Keep replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials in a separate safe cache. This evidence demonstrates one failure sequence; the exact corruption threshold and universal Chamber-disable rules remain unverified. Update 1 evidence also states that death drops every carried weapon, including the pistol.

Starry Night is about 1/5 difficulty with zero persistent hostile spawn markers within 250 units, although roaming enemies can wander in. Clear wanderers and open the final chest first. Its guaranteed value is the Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module.

claims.value: Player-facing hierarchy: Mission Timeline is the player-selected visual source of truth. Its portrait monitor keeps five layers visible without scrolling: (1) synchronization/capability status, including degraded or unsynced state and sound, haptic, notification, loud-alarm, and screen-awake status; (2) a semantic hero state, huge monospaced countdown, and explicit countdown target; (3) threat instruction plus one action sentence; (4) no more than two opportunity cards above the fold; and (5) exact-local-time next events with only Mute one cycle and Re-sync permanently exposed. The five mission bands are Fire wave 0:00-0:30, Remain sheltered, counting to Cooling; Cooling 0:30-1:30, Remain sheltered, counting to Recovery; Recovery/QUIET WINDOW 1:30-11:30, Lower ambient risk—triggered encounters may persist, counting to expected ordinary Vermin return; World active 11:30-51:30, ordinary hostiles expected, counting to Ruptura warning; and Ruptura warning 51:30-54:00, Return, bank loot, and shelter, counting to impact. Thus the hero is always the next meaningful event, not elapsed time or a generic phase: during recovery it is expected ordinary-Vermin return; during active ecology it is warning start; during warning it is impact. The recovery period is only a lower-threat opportunity window because Geo Scanner, monolith, infection, Base Core, scripted POI, and other triggered encounters may ignore the environmental cycle. Retain one proportional whole-cycle rail for orientation, but pair it with minimum/equal-width labeled steps or a next-event list so the 30-second Fire wave and 60-second Cooling phases never collapse into unusable slivers. Color remains supporting atmosphere: text, symbols, borders, and instructions carry state independently.

claims.value: Alert/native-iOS safety boundary: enemy-return and Ruptura alerts require distinct sounds and haptic signatures and must never rely on color or audio alone. Enemy-return defaults are 5 minutes (amber edge, Finish or leave hard POIs, short double haptic/optional tone, normal notification), 2 minutes (persistent retreat banner, double tone/haptic, optional notification), 1 minute (red instruction and emphasized seconds, background notification off by default), 15 seconds (static danger border, large seconds, one final cue with no ticking and no background notification), and the event (ORDINARY VERMIN RETURNING, urgent triple cue, local notification or explicitly armed alarm). Ruptura offers optional 10-minute planning, then 5 minutes, warning start at 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact. Support an exit buffer, Full/Haptic only/Visual only profiles, separate phase/enemy/Ruptura/opportunity toggles, Mute one cycle, and preview before the first session. On resume or clock correction, never replay missed thresholds: recompute current state and collapse the backlog to one strongest current-state message; the preserved planner uses a 5_000-millisecond foreground freshness threshold, suppresses historical presentation on resume/clock correction, and identifies occurrences by sync epoch, definition ID, event ID, and cycle index. Schedule ordinary local notifications at absolute dates and replace them after anchor/model/policy changes; recompute from (now - anchor) modulo cycle duration on resume and deduplicate by cycle plus event ID. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor scene is active and restore it afterward; provide dim OLED mode, recommend charging, and never use background audio as a keep-alive. A Live Activity represents only the currently armed event, not an indefinitely self-advancing promise. AlarmKit loud behavior is opt-in per app and per deliberately armed Watch Session/next event; never create an endless 54-minute alarm. Earlier iOS uses normal local notifications, Time Sensitive is separately opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Accessibility requires text/symbol/border or pattern alongside color, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, no full-screen flashing transition, no default per-second ticking, one stable VoiceOver sentence rather than per-second announcements, and haptics only as a complement.
